A parameter record fixes a sample size \(n\ge 1\), an order pair \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) with
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad r\ge 2,
\]
a comparison exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), positive constants
\[
 C_{\theta},\ C_g,\ C_q,\ \psi_{\eta},\ \psi_{\xi},\ \delta,\ \sigma>0,
\]
and two code-radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative and nonincreasing on positive indices; their values at \(n\) are written \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).

Two conventions are used throughout: \(N(m,v)\) denotes the Gaussian law on \(\mathbb R\) with mean \(m\) and variance \(v\), and \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(O_i)\) denotes the empirical average of \(f\) over the sample.  The sample is split into the two deterministic folds
\[
 I_0=\{i:i<\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad I_1=\{i:i\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\]
written \(I_a\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\).

For a real random variable \(W\) and \(t>0\), the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian convention is that \(\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}\le t\) means \(E[\exp(W^2/t^2)]\le 2\), and its conditional form \(\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le t\) means \(E[\exp(W^2/t^2)\mid X]\le 2\) almost surely.

An observation is the triple \(O=(X,T,Y)\), where \(X\) takes values in a measurable covariate space \(\mathcal X\) and \(T,Y\in\mathbb R\).  A model over a parameter record consists of a probability law \(P\) for \(O\) under which \(T\) and \(Y\) are integrable, a real coefficient \(\theta_0\), measurable regression functions \(g_0,q_0\) on the covariate space with
\[
 g_0(X)=E_P[T\mid X],\qquad q_0(X)=E_P[Y\mid X]
\]
\(P\)-almost surely, and deterministic measurable supplied code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) for \(g_0\) and \(q_0\).  The treatment and outcome innovations are
\[
 \eta=T-g_0(X),\qquad \xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta,
\]
and the clipped supplied codes at index \(n\) are
\[
 \bar g_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},\qquad
 \bar q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
The covariate marginal of \(P\) is written \(P_X\).  A model is written \(m\), and when the law has to be displayed the coefficient is written \(\theta_0(P)\).

Let \(P\) be an observed-data law, let \(n\ge 1\), and let \(W=W(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) be a real-valued statistic of the sample.  Under the i.i.d. product law \(P^{\otimes n}\) write \(F_W(t)=\Pr(W\le t)\) for the distribution function of \(W\). \[
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\ F_W(t)\ge 1-\gamma\},
\]
the left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F_W\) evaluated at level \(1-\gamma\).

The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification.  A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
 x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
 \qquad
 I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) with \(p\le x\).  Executable code may inspect only the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.  It may not inspect a semantic exact-real value.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
 A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
 \qquad
 A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
\[
 A B=
 [\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
  \max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\).  Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
 (A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), put
\[
 \operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
 \min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Thus \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds.  Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures: after \(q\) bisections their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\).  This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds.  Division is the guarded operation
\[
 \frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
 =(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
and is executed only when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed, rather than postulated, from Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
 \arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
 \qquad
 |R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures.  If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), so this is an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations.  The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
 3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
 N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\).  Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested.  Hence
\[
 \exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle.  Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
 r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive.  If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell.  Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations therefore yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures.  Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations.  Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) only if it implements these algorithms, exports their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiles the resulting module.  This definition is the explicit bounded-build obligation; it does not state or imply that the missing complex operations are already exported by Causalean.  Until such an implementation is added and compiled, later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.

Let \(p\) be a parameter record with sample size \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(1\le n\), orders \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(2\le r\), exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) satisfying \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma>0\), and sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\varepsilon_\ell(t)\ge0\) for \(t\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon_\ell(j)\le\varepsilon_\ell(i)\) whenever \(1\le i\le j\), for \(\ell=1,2\). Let \(\operatorname{Name}(x)\) denote a supplied certified-real record with value \(x\), and let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote such a record together with a rational lower-bound witness \(\ell>0\) satisfying \(\ell\le x\). As part of the experiment convention, fix the supplied record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k_{\star},\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k_{\star}\) is exact with \(k_{\star}=k\) and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1).
\]
The value contracts are
\[
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Writing \(A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}\) for the numerical factor, this reads \(R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\).
The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is the primitive certified input shared by the bank and the estimator for this parameter record.  The bank data assembled below from \(p\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is written \(B\).

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one. If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), define
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J_{\mathrm{base}}=2^{m_{\star}-1}.
\]
The bank therefore contains
\[
 J=J_{\mathrm{base}}+1
\]
circles, indexed by \(j\in\{0,\ldots,J_{\mathrm{base}}\}\).
For each \(j=0,\ldots,J_{\mathrm{base}}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+j2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_j
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+j2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
The associated real-valued radius field is
\[
 \rho_j=(\mathfrak\rho_j).\operatorname{value}
       =R_0+1/4+j2^{-m_{\star}}.
\]

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}).
\]
Define the rational dyadic certificate and its real value by
\[
 a_{\star,\mathbb Q}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0,
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=(a_{\star,\mathbb Q}:\mathbb R).
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, certified additions with rational point records, and primitive recursion over the displayed integer bounds. The construction is a finite certified procedure in the supplied record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\).

The construction has a mathematical layer and a represented-data layer, both relative to exactly the same experiment-wide parameter and primitive records.

Let \(\mathcal X\) be a measurable covariate space. Fix a parameter record \(p\) consisting of a positive sample size \(n\), natural numbers \(r\) and \(k\) with \(k=r+1\) and \(2\le r\), an exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(r\le s\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and two sequences \(\varepsilon_{1n},\varepsilon_{2n}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative on positive indices and nonincreasing there: for \(\ell\ge1\), \(0\le\varepsilon_{1n}(\ell)\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_{2n}(\ell)\), and whenever \(1\le a\le b\), \(\varepsilon_{1n}(b)\le\varepsilon_{1n}(a)\) and \(\varepsilon_{2n}(b)\le\varepsilon_{2n}(a)\). Fix a deterministic treatment-regression code sequence; the estimator records measurability of its current \(n\)th code as its public-domain proposition.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from the contour-bank handle: its natural-name field equals \(k\), its positive certified-real fields represent \(\delta\), \(\psi_{\eta}\), \(R_0\), and \(R_1\), and its value contracts are
\[
 R_0=A_k\left(\frac{\psi_{\eta}^2}{\delta}\right)^{(k-2)^{-1}},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Once for all, fix one actual range record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed for the estimator before the law or sample varies, and they remain the primitive names used throughout the construction.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records, where \(\bar g_n\) is the projection of the current treatment-regression code onto \([-C_g,C_g]\). Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\). The ordinary program is the resulting finite-rational result, the full trace is its trace field, and the ordinary value is the projection of its raw rational output onto the fixed certified range \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\). This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record. The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation.

At the represented-data layer, callers supply the observation record
\[
 \widetilde{\mathfrak s}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied certified digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\). The represented program forms the full internal input
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr)
\]
by adjoining the displayed fixed primitive components. For each supplied compiled bounded spectral adapter, consisting of the build together with pilot-boundary, winding-quadrature, and evaluation-quadrature entry points satisfying their exact correspondence contracts with the built finite programs, the represented program applies those entry points to this full internal input. Its output-correspondence proposition asserts that, for every ordinary data set, the represented result on the canonical represented input equals the ordinary finite-rational result, the two traces are equal, and the represented output name certifies the ordinary clipped value.

Invoke the contour-bank handle on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction. At every certified circle node, use the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\). Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below. With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
The integrand \(V_j\) is NOT normalized at this stage: the certified zero count \(N_j\) divides the finished mesh enclosure, not the integrand.
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 64\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 64\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
Both displays carry the rational constant \(64\) rather than the analytically tight factor coming from \(dz_j/dt\): the whole mesh schedule is evaluated in \(\mathbb Q\), so the certified Lipschitz constant must itself be rational, and enlarging it only refines the mesh.
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations. Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\). If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\). That integral is the winding number of \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) along \(C_j\); write
\[
 N_j=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz,
\]
which by the argument principle counts, with multiplicity, the zeros of \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) enclosed by \(C_j\). Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle. A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\). Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if the admissible set is empty.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\). Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature enclose the unnormalized integral
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz,
\]
and dividing that enclosure by \(N_j\) afterwards gives a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of the real interval of that normalized rectangle, represented by its rational point name. Projection uses certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation to construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the program output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break. Identical ordinary samples with the same parameter, treatment-regression code sequence, and fixed primitive records have identical ordinary traces and output records; identical represented observation records with the same fixed primitive records and the same compiled bounded spectral adapter have identical represented traces and output records. The value represented by the ordinary output is, by definition, the ordinary-sample statistic evaluated with the same fixed primitive records. The procedure uses \(\bar g_n\). The ordinary program, ordinary value, and full trace are defined directly by the canonical represented input and the finite rational adapter; the represented output correspondence is the stated contract for each supplied compiled bounded spectral adapter.

Fix a parameter record \(p\) consisting of a positive sample size \(n\), natural numbers \(r\) and \(k\) with \(k=r+1\) and \(2\le r\), an exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(r\le s\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and two sequences \(\varepsilon_{1n},\varepsilon_{2n}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative on positive indices and nonincreasing there: for \(\ell\ge1\), \(0\le\varepsilon_{1n}(\ell)\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_{2n}(\ell)\), and whenever \(1\le a\le b\), \(\varepsilon_{1n}(b)\le\varepsilon_{1n}(a)\) and \(\varepsilon_{2n}(b)\le\varepsilon_{2n}(a)\). Fix a deterministic treatment-regression code sequence; the estimator records measurability of its current \(n\)th code as its public-domain proposition.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from the contour-bank handle: its natural-name field equals \(k\), its positive certified-real fields represent \(\delta\), \(\psi_{\eta}\), \(R_0\), and \(R_1\), and its value contracts are
\[
 R_0=A_k\left(\frac{\psi_{\eta}^2}{\delta}\right)^{(k-2)^{-1}},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Once for all, fix one actual range record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed for the estimator before the law or sample varies, and they remain the primitive names used throughout the construction.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records, where \(\bar g_n\) is the projection of the current treatment-regression code onto \([-C_g,C_g]\). Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\). The ordinary program is the resulting finite-rational result, the full trace is its trace field, and the ordinary value is the projection of its raw rational output onto the fixed certified range \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\). This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record. The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation.

At the represented-data layer, callers supply the observation record
\[
 \widetilde{\mathfrak s}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied certified digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\). The represented program forms the full internal input
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr)
\]
by adjoining the displayed fixed primitive components. For each supplied compiled bounded spectral adapter, consisting of the build together with pilot-boundary, winding-quadrature, and evaluation-quadrature entry points satisfying their exact correspondence contracts with the built finite programs, the represented program applies those entry points to this full internal input. Its output-correspondence proposition asserts that, for every ordinary data set, the represented result on the canonical represented input equals the ordinary finite-rational result, the two traces are equal, and the represented output name certifies the ordinary clipped value.

Invoke the contour-bank handle on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction. At every certified circle node, use the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\). Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below. With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
The integrand \(V_j\) is NOT normalized at this stage: the certified zero count \(N_j\) divides the finished mesh enclosure, not the integrand.
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 64\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 64\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
Both displays carry the rational constant \(64\) rather than the analytically tight factor coming from \(dz_j/dt\): the whole mesh schedule is evaluated in \(\mathbb Q\), so the certified Lipschitz constant must itself be rational, and enlarging it only refines the mesh.
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations. Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\). If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\). That integral is the winding number of \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) along \(C_j\); write
\[
 N_j=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz,
\]
which by the argument principle counts, with multiplicity, the zeros of \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) enclosed by \(C_j\). Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle. A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\). Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if the admissible set is empty.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\). Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature enclose the unnormalized integral
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz,
\]
and dividing that enclosure by \(N_j\) afterwards gives a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of the real interval of that normalized rectangle, represented by its rational point name. Projection uses certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation to construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the program output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break. Identical ordinary samples with the same parameter, treatment-regression code sequence, and fixed primitive records have identical ordinary traces and output records; identical represented observation records with the same fixed primitive records and the same compiled bounded spectral adapter have identical represented traces and output records. The value represented by the ordinary output is, by definition, the ordinary-sample statistic evaluated with the same fixed primitive records. The procedure uses \(\bar g_n\). The ordinary program, ordinary value, and full trace are defined directly by the canonical represented input and the finite rational adapter; the represented output correspondence is the stated contract for each supplied compiled bounded spectral adapter.

nl.statement:
Use the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian convention of \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}; the lemma is applied with \(W=\eta\) and \(\psi=\psi_{\eta}\). Let \(\psi>0\) and let \(W\) be a real-valued measurable function on a probability space carrying the law \(P\), with \(W\in L^1(P)\), \(E_PW=0\), \(\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\in L^1(P)\), and \(E_P\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\le2\). Then, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_Pe^{tW}\le\exp(4\psi^2t^2).
\]
The proof splits on the scale \(|t\psi|\). In the small-scale regime \(|t\psi|\le1\), the exponential Taylor remainder bound \(e^u\le1+u+u^2e^{|u|}\), the elementary inequality \(|tW|\le\{(t\psi)^2+(W/\psi)^2\}/2\le\{1+(W/\psi)^2\}/2\), and the bound \(y^2e^{(1+y^2)/2}\le2e^{y^2}\) give the pointwise estimate
\[
e^{tW}\le1+tW+2(t\psi)^2\exp(W^2/\psi^2),
\]
which integrates to \(1+4(t\psi)^2\le\exp(4\psi^2t^2)\). In the large-scale regime \(|t\psi|>1\), the inequality \(tW\le(t\psi)^2/4+W^2/\psi^2\) integrates to \(E_Pe^{tW}\le2\exp\{(t\psi)^2/4\}\le\exp(4\psi^2t^2)\).

nl.statement:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants
\(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]
For every parameter record \(p\) whose constants
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) are the ones just fixed, and every \(n\ge 1\), if the non-Gaussian class in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} is nonempty, then there are a base law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed observed treatment law.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) equals its law under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed regressions and supplied codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) equal those under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome equation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\).
\item \textbf{(Product relative entropy.)} For all real \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and
\[
|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=\frac{h}{\sqrt n},
\]
one has
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Moreover, for every starting law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the class of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, there is a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(JMS ACE membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed observed treatment law.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) equals its law under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed nuisance objects.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), and the treatment innovation \(\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) equal those under \(P^{\circ}\), and the treatment and outcome code-radius conditions in \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} hold at \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome equation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
\item \textbf{(Product relative entropy.)} For all real \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and
\[
|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=\frac{h}{\sqrt n},
\]
one has
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Finally, for every pair of clipped-code functions \(g_{\star},q_{\star}:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), if there is a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n=g_{\star}\) and \(\bar q_n=q_{\star}\), then the fixed-code JMS ACE minimax risk satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\ \bar g_n=g_{\star},\ \bar q_n=q_{\star}}}
E_P\!\left[\{\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\}^2\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed regressions and supplied codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) equal those under \(P^{\circ}\).

\[

\[

\]

\le

Write \(B\) for the contour bank generated by \(p\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), with dyadic lower-modulus certificate \(a_{\star}\), circles \(C_j\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-functional} of radius \(\rho_j\), and outer radius \(R_1\); write \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) for the total Borel contour statistic of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, computed with the certified interval arithmetic of \cref{obj:def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate} on the canonicalized sample, and write \(\widehat F_{1,n},\widehat G_{1,n}\) for the evaluation-fold empirical transforms of \cref{obj:def:local-gaussian-handle}. Let \(F,G:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\) be arbitrary functions, let \(d,e,C_G,\mu,\nu\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|\vartheta|\le C_{\theta}\). Assume the canonical selector good event: \(d\ge0\), \(e\ge0\), \(C_G\ge0\), \(\mu=31a_{\star}/64>0\), \(\nu=23a_{\star}/64>0\), \(d\le\mu-\nu\), and there are a bank index \(j\) and an integer \(N_j\ge1\) such that the program selects the circle \(C_j\), the pilot winding rectangle at \(C_j\) decodes to \(N_j\), the evaluation-fold modulus enclosure at \(C_j\) has lower endpoint at least \(a_{\star}/4\), and every \(z\) with \(|z|=\rho_j\) satisfies \(\mu\le|F(z)|\), \(|G(z)|\le C_G\), \(|\widehat F_{1,n}(z)-F(z)|\le d\), and \(|\widehat G_{1,n}(z)-G(z)|\le e\). \[

\le

\le

\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \{4R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\}^{-1},
\]

\[
\frac{c}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
E_P\!\left[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n},

\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}.
\]
\end{itemize}

\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\).  There is a constant
\(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that
the following statements hold.

Let \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the constant in the
published order-\(r\) ACE generalized-quantile guarantee, and write
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) for the estimator supplied by that
published ACE handle.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter record whose
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(\gamma\)
coordinates equal the displayed constants, and fix the certified primitive
bank and range records associated with \(p_0\).  For any parameter record
\(p\) sharing the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and the same
probability level \(\gamma\), and for any supplied code sequences whose clipped
versions are \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\), the following hold, under the
usual measurability and integrability conditions.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Class relations.} At the sample size \(n\) of \(p\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If the comparison exponent of \(p\) satisfies \(s=r\), then the common clipped-code convention gives
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
Here the classes and the comparison subclass are those of
\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}.

\item \textbf{ACE upper guarantee.} If a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
uses the clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\),
if the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of
\cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility,obj:def:jms-eligibility-quantities} holds,
and if \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \bigl(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|\bigr)
 \le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}\) is the generalized quantile in
\cref{obj:def:generalized-quantile} and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
 &= C_{\gamma} r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   + C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}  \\
 &\qquad\qquad
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
   \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains at least one law using
the clipped supplied codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds,
\(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}
 \le
 \{4R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1\) is the outer contour radius of \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle} determined by the parameter record in force,
then the certified contour statistic
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of
\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed primitive

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} The treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has the law of
\[
\eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) are independent.
\item \textbf{(Sampling and model restrictions.)} The law satisfies \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}.
\item \textbf{(Current treatment-code radius.)} For the clipped supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\),
\[
\int |\,\bar g_n(x)-g_0(x)\,|\,dP_X(x)\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
under the usual integrability condition for this \(L^1(P_X)\) quantity.
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},\qquad
A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},\qquad
\Delta_a=2a^4.
\]
Then the treatment-innovation moment-generating function satisfies
\[
M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
\]
the fourth cumulant satisfies \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4\), and \(t_a>0\) is the first positive zero of the characteristic transform: \(M_a(it_a)=0\) and \(M_a(iu)\ne0\) for every \(u\in(0,t_a)\).  Moreover, for every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{t_a(\eta+d)\}]=0.
\]

\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]

\]

\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/2.
\]

\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}

 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}

Let \(n\ge1\), let \(W\) and \(R\) be real-valued functions of a single observation \(O\), and let \(\theta,C_{\theta},A,\mu_W\) be real numbers with \(|\theta|\le C_{\theta}\), \(A>0\), and \(\mu_W\ge A/2\). Then, for every sample of size \(n\),
\[
(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2
\le
\frac{16}{A^2}\left\{(\mathbb P_nR)^2+C_{\theta}^2(\mathbb P_nW-\mu_W)^2\right\}.
\]
The bound is deterministic and is proved by splitting on the threshold: in the good-denominator case \(A/4\le\mathbb P_nW\) the clipping is contractive around \(\theta\) and the ratio error equals \(\mathbb P_nR/\mathbb P_nW\), while in the bad-denominator case \(\widehat\theta=0\) and the deviation obeys \(A/4\le\mu_W-\mathbb P_nW\), so the constant loss \(\theta^2\le C_{\theta}^2\) is absorbed by the second term.
